 Oral Judgment

The injured/claimant is in appeal challenging the judgment and award dated 1.10.2014 passed in MVC No.118/2013 on the file of learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and Member, Addl. MACT,
Haveri1.
2.

Principal Senior Civil Judge and Member, Addl. MACT,
Haveri1
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel Sri. Harish S Maigur for the appellant/claimant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in dismissing the claim petition on the ground that the appellant himself was a tort-feasor.

It is submitted that the Tribunal ought to have taken note of the fact that the claim petition was filed under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 19882, where question of proving negligence would not arise.
Hence, he seeks to allow the appeal.

3. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. S.S. Koliwad for the respondent/insurer would submit that the appellant was borrower of the vehicle from the owner of the motorcycle i.e. respondent No.1 and due to negligence of the appellant/rider, the accident has caused, hence, question of paying any 'Tribunal', for short 'MV Act, 1988', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11402 compensation to the tort-feasor would not arise.
Thus, he seeks dismissal of the appeal.
4. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record including original records of the Tribunal.

5. It is not in dispute that in a road accident on 19.08.2007, the appellant was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-27/K-8629, at that time, he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries.
Due to the injuries sustained in the said accident, he filed claim petition under Section 163-A of the MV Act, 1988 seeking compensation.
The Tribunal taking note of the fact that the appellant was negligent/tort-feasor dismissed the claim petition.
There is no dispute with regard to the said preposition of law.
However, the insurance policy on record indicates that in case of personal accident, insurance company is liable to pay a sum of Rs.1 lakhs as compensation.
It is evident that PA coverage is available to the rider of the motorcycle i.e., the appellant herein.

6. The said issue has been considered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ramkhiladi Vs. The United India Insurance NC: 2024:KHC-D:11402 Company Limited & Another3, wherein paragraph-5.6 reads as under:
"5.6.

entities.text: Ramkhiladi Vs. The United India Insurance NC: 2024:KHC-D:11402 Company Limited & Another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In view of the above and for the reasons stated above, in the present case, as the claim under Section 163A of the Act was made only against the owner and insurance Anand @ Anandkumar S/O Ankaleppa ... vs Sureshgowda S/O Neelappagowda Patil on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/227970/
2 company of the vehicle which was being driven by the deceased himself as borrower of the vehicle from the owner of the vehicle and he would be in the shoes of the owner, the High Court has rightly observed and held that such a claim was not maintainable and the claimants ought to have joined and/or ought to have made the claim under Section 163A of the Act against the driver, owner and/or the insurance company of the offending vehicle i.e. RJ 29 2M 9223 being a third party to the said vehicle."

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Taking note of enunciation of law laid down referred supra, I am of the considered view that the rejection of claim petition by the Tribunal under Section 163-A of the MV Act, 1988 is justifiable,
however, policy on record further indicates that the policy has covered for personal accident of owner.
Hence, the appellant/rider, who stepped into shoes of the owner, is entitled to compensation of Rs.1 lakh.

To buttress the same, it would be useful to refer paragraph-5.8 of the judgment in Ramkhiladi supra, which reads as under:
"5.8.
However, at the same time, even as per the contract of insurance, in case of personal accident the ownerdriver is entitled to a sum of Rs.1 lakh.
Therefore, the deceased, as observed hereinabove, who would be in the shoes of the owner shall be entitled to a sum of Rs.1 lakh, even as per the contract of insurance.

However, it is the case on behalf of the original claimants that there is an amendment to the 2 nd 2020 (2) SCC 550 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11402 Schedule and a fixed amount of Rs.5 lakh has been specified in case of death and therefore the claimants shall be entitled to Rs.5 lakh.
The same cannot be accepted.

In the present case, the accident took place in the year 2006 and even the Judgment and Award was passed by the learned Tribunal in the year 2009, and the impugned Judgment and Order has been passed by the High Court in 10.05.2018, i.e. much prior to the amendment in the 2nd Schedule.
In the facts and circumstance of the present case, the claimants shall not be entitled to the benefit of the amendment to the 2 nd Schedule.
At the same time, as observed hereinabove, the claimants shall be entitled to Rs.1 lakh as per the terms of the contract of insurance, the driver being in the shoes of the owner of the vehicle.

5.9 Now, so far as the submission made on behalf of the claimants that in a claim under Section 163A of the Act mere use of the vehicle is enough and despite the compensation claimed by the heirs of the owner of the motorcycle which was involved in the accident resulting in his death, the claim under Section 163A of the Act would be maintainable is concerned, in view of the decision of this Court in Rajni Devi (supra), the aforesaid cannot be accepted.

In Rajni Devi (supra), it has been specifically observed and held that the provisions of Section 163A of the Act cannot be said to have any application with regard to an accident wherein the owner of the motor vehicle himself is involved.

After considering the decisions of this Court in the cases of Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Jhuma Saha (2007) 9 SCC 263; Dhanraj (supra); National Insurance Co. Ltd. V. Laxmi Narain Dhut (2007) 3 SCC 700 and Premkumari v. Prahlad Dev (2008) 3 SCC 193, it is ultimately concluded by this Court that the liability under Section 163A of the Act is on the owner of the vehicle as a person cannot be both, a claimant as also a recipient and, therefore, the heirs of the Anand @ Anandkumar S/O Ankaleppa ... vs Sureshgowda S/O Neelappagowda Patil on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/227970/
3 owner could not have maintained the claim in terms of Section 163A of the Act.

sentences.text: It is further observed that, for the said purpose, only the terms of the contract of insurance could be taken recourse to.

In the recent decision of this Court in the case of Ashalata Bhowmik (supra), it is specifically held by this Court that the parties shall be governed by the terms and conditions of the contract of insurance.

Therefore, as per the contract of insurance, the insurance company shall be liable to pay the compensation to a third party and not to the owner, except to the extent of Rs.1 lakh as observed hereinabove."
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11402 8.
In view of enunciation of law referred supra, the appeal filed by the claimant is allowed in part.

The respondent/Insurance company is liable to pay a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- as compensation to the appellant/claimant along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
The said amount shall be deposited before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
On such deposit, the same shall be paid to the appellant/claimant on proper identification.
Registry shall transmit the TCR to the Tribunal forthwith.
Draw modified award accordingly.
